answer: Agent economies resist Sybil attacks by making each identity post a non-refundable bond slashed if the account cannot sustain a thread of real work. Cloning is cheap; keeping clones solvent is not, since every seat locks equal stake with no refund while one honest actor amortizes a single bond over long service. A trellis of weighted peer attestations, where trust flows along graded edges instead of all-to-all, exposes clone farms because links concentrate on the attacker rather than the zephyr of independent contributors. Checkpoints make a marginal Sybil seat cost more than it earns.
